classification: Historical site assessment demonstration. This data file is not a hydrology model, a benefit-transfer assessment, or a cost ledger.

sources.title: City of Kyle Weekly Report, August 22, 2025
sources.statement: Conservation staff assessed 5 acres at Waterleaf Park; invasive grasses dominated the site and native revegetation was planned.

sources.title: City of Kyle Weekly Report, December 5, 2025
sources.statement: Report documents treatment of invasive King Ranch bluestem and application of a custom native seed mix using a no-till drill.

sources.title: Land Management Tracking Form, Waterleaf LMU 1/2, operations dated November 18, 2025
sources.statement: Internal records report seeding operations but no public underlying file or certified geometry is available.

claims.limitation: Area assessed for planning, NOT a surveyed restored or modeled area.
Invasive grasses reported to dominate; no baseline species-cover percentage or controlled survey.

claims.endpoint: Reported invasive King Ranch bluestem treatment and no-till native seeding
claims.limitation: Report date is not necessarily application date. No yield, germination, cover, or soil improvement measured.
Sum of two internally logged units (1.86 and 3.15 acres), not public survey geometry and NOT identical by assumption to poster's 3.6-acre accounting area.
Two internal entries (40 and 69 lb), not independently verified material receipts or native plant establishment.

disallowed_calculations: Do not treat 5 assessed acres or 5.01 internally logged acres as a validated runoff-model footprint.
Do not treat a reported seeding operation as documented successful establishment or incremental ecosystem benefit.
Do not treat promotional poster ecosystem-service dollars, restoration costs, or returns as verified project outcomes.
Do not turn statewide benefit-transfer totals into site-specific incremental gains without a compatible baseline.
next_measurements: Publicly releasable GIS polygon for assessed, seeded and financially evaluated extents, with distinct boundaries.
Matched vegetation surveys (native/exotic percent cover and structure) and repeatable protocol.
Documented soil map unit, compaction or infiltration and modeled annual runoff under both conditions.
Dated detailed mowing labor/equipment records and actual restoration costs, before and after.
Documented baseline/post-treatment carbon and biodiversity monitoring if those benefits will be claimed.
